ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Given the function $y=2x+b$ and the function $y=kx-3$ intersect at point $P(4, -6)$, what is the solution set of the inequality $kx-3>2x+b$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\[ \text{{\bf Solution:}} \, \text{Given that the function} \, y=2x+b \, \text{and the function} \, y=kx-3 \, \text{intersect at point} \, P(4,-6), \]
\[ \text{therefore, the solution set of the inequality} \, kx-3>2x+b \, \text{is} \, \boxed{x<4}. \]

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Given the function $y=2x+b$ and the function $y=kx-3$ intersect at point $P(4,-6)$, what is the solution set of the inequality $kx-3>2x+b$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: From the text, the two lines y=2x+b and y=kx-3 intersect at P(4,-6), so P lies on both lines. Substitute P into y=2x+b: -6=2·4+b, so -6=8+b and b=-14. Substitute P into y=kx-3: -6=4k-3, so -3=4k and k=-3/4. Now solve kx-3>2x+b: (-3/4)x-3>2x-14. Add 14 to both sides: (-3/4)x+11>2x. Move x-terms to the right: 11>2x+(3/4)x=(11/4)x. Since 11/4 is positive, divide both sides by 11/4 to get 4>x, i.e. x<4.
